data.title: Břeclav – Pohansko, a Great Moravian centre on the Dyje
data.excerpt: Pohansko lies on the left bank of the river Dyje about 4 km south of Břeclav: a fortified settlement of the lowland type covering 27 ha, or up to 100 ha with its suburbia. Built at the beginning of the 9th century and abandoned in the 11th, it has yielded a three-aisled church with some 400 graves, a magnate's court, a craft settlement and a pagan sanctuary.
data.metaTitle: Břeclav – Pohansko, a Great Moravian hillfort
data.metaDescription: A Great Moravian hillfort on the Dyje covering 27 ha, up to 100 ha with its suburbia, built early in the 9th century — a monument of European importance.

children.text: The hillfort lies close to the Moravian–Austrian state border on the left bank of the river Dyje, about 4 km to the south of Břeclav. It covers 27 ha and, together with several suburbia, occupies an area of up to 100 ha. It was built at the beginning of the 9th century. In addition, several separate settlements of the same period have been discovered in the surroundings of Pohansko. At some point in the 11th century the hillfort was abandoned altogether and forgotten. It acquired the name “Pohansko” only later, when people found various objects here which they believed had been left behind by some ancient pagan people. It can be counted among the most important monuments of the early Middle Ages not only in the Czech Republic but in the whole of Central Europe.

Early Slavic and Early Hillfort-period occupation (6th–8th century) was recorded at two places in the northern part of the hillfort. Over the course of three centuries the clustered settlement, divided into individual farmsteads, gradually shifted. A contemporary inhumation cemetery was investigated to the south of the settlement.

children.text: We class it among fortified settlements of the lowland type. The defensive ramparts of the hillfort were 2 km long and up to 25 m wide, so they must have been very high. It is therefore one of the largest early medieval fortifications in Central Europe. The fortified area of the hillfort was moreover protected on all sides by the river Dyje and its branches. The foundations of a larger church decorated with coloured frescoes were uncovered at the hillfort. The church was three-aisled, 18.6 m long and 7.2 m wide. A large cemetery was discovered around the church; approximately 400 graves containing 800 artefacts were uncovered. Four magnates' graves with swords were found here, and the graves held a quantity of gold and silver jewellery and

of a similar character to those found in the graves at the hillfort between Kopčany and Mikulčice and at Staré Město. The finds and graves come mostly from the second half of the 9th century. No grave reaches beneath the foundations of the church, so the church was built first and only then was burial carried out here. The church fell out of use at some point in the 11th to 12th century.

In the north-western part of the hillfort a magnate's court was identified: a rectangular settlement unit almost 1 ha in area, enclosed by a wooden palisade and built in two phases in the 9th century. Inside the court there was a sacral precinct with a church and a burial ground, a residential precinct with single-roomed as well as multi-roomed houses on stone and mortar footings, and a farm section with pens and sties, a barn, granaries and so on.

Besides the court, further extensive Great Moravian settlement areas and a smaller cemetery were investigated at various places inside the hillfort and in the bailey. The craft settlement in the north-eastern part of the hillfort (in the former forest nursery about 100 m east of the excavation of the magnate's court) was investigated over an area of more than 2 ha without its edges being reached (260 Great Moravian features). On the basis of the finds, various kinds of craft can be documented at the settlement: for example the working of wood, leather and furs, bone-working, the working of non-ferrous metals, smithing, jewellery-making and textile production. During the 2008 excavation season the foundations of another stone building, laid in mortar, were uncovered in this area; it too is presumed to have had a sacral purpose.

The Great Moravian settlement area of the southern bailey forms three clusters whose ground plans are determined by the sunken-featured dwellings. The eastern one (with a stone-built well in the middle) perhaps had a craft and production character. The middle one (with a row-like to street-like arrangement, with storage spaces, abundant finds of querns and the like) may have been a hamlet of court servants of various categories. The western one (with finds of riding equipment) was evidently a hamlet of the military retinue available to the magnate — a princely dignitary — whose seat was in the court at the hillfort.

An Old Slavic pagan sanctuary was also discovered at Pohansko during the archaeological excavations. It is a post-built feature of the first half of the 10th century, consisting of 8 perimeter postholes arranged around a central one and enclosed by a palisade which forms a circle 260 cm in diameter, left open for about a quarter of its circumference. A reconstruction of this sanctuary stands in the archaeological open-air museum established in the grounds of the hillfort. The sanctuary is built on the spot where it was discovered and corresponds in its overall shape to the original feature. The palisade is open towards the point of sunrise on the day of the summer solstice (21 June). The feature served a cult function, but it may also have served as a primitive calendar.
